text:
elaine: Heads up — I ran initial bring-up for mpt-7b-q4f16 (PTQ). Quick numbers below, and I need product/GTN guidance on whether we should recommend this for chat vs high-throughput completions. TL;DR: ~2.5x cost savings, ~3-4% convQA drop.

sam: Can you paste the eval table + baseline?

elaine: baseline: ref-model-7b (fp16)
qmodel: mpt-7b-q4f16
latency p95: fp16=180ms, q=130ms
tokens/sec: fp16=320, q=760
token cost: fp16=$0.0009/token, q=$0.00036/token
convQA EM: fp16=72.4, q=69.6 (-2.8)
code-sum BLEU: fp16=41.2, q=40.1 (-1.1)
hallucination suite: fp16=3.1%, q=6.8%
notes: PTQ used, measured w/ KV caching on, 2048 context p95.

miguel: Which eval sets are these? OOD or internal?

elaine: Internal convQA v2 (3k QAs) + synthetic code-summarization (1k). Also ran our hallucination suite (~500 cases).

fiona: Were these runs with KV caching enabled? Quantization can degrade long-context behaviors.

elaine: Yes KV caching on. p95 latency measured on 2048 seq.

sam: Product framing Q: Given latency and cost wins, are we comfortable recommending for customer-facing chat? Maybe recommend for non-critical high-throughput routes (batch embeddings, summarization, code-assist) first. :thinking_face:  

miguel: Also worth doing a QAT experiment — could recover quality while keeping most of the cost benefit. PTQ is cheaper but quality hit is visible.

elaine: Agreed. PTQ only so far. QAT would need retrain budget & infra. Would like ops estimates.

fiona: Can you share hallucination examples? Absolute rate increase seems concerning (3.1 -> 6.8%).

elaine: Quick examples: longer multi-step reasoning prompts produced more invented facts. Short QA still fine. I'll paste one example in #eng-ml later.

sam: Proposed recommendation (scorecard row): cost_delta=-60%, latency_delta=-28%, EM_delta=-3.8, hall_rate_delta=+3.7. Action: "Recommend for non-critical high-throughput routes; run QAT experiment; canary to 5% with fallback to fp16 if hallucination >5%".

miguel: Also add unit economics per 1M tokens/day: cost_fp16=$900/day, cost_q=$360/day => savings $540/day. Put that on the GTN slide.

elaine: I'll draft a 1-page scorecard + short JSON metrics for GTN. Proposing canary gating: EM drop <=4% AND hallucination increase <=2% to graduate to larger traffic.

ops-bot: Deployed canary target 'mpt-7b-q4f16-canary' to staging with 5% traffic at ts=1753502700 :rocket:

fiona: Nice. One more ask — include per-route latency budgets and an automatic fallback policy to fp16 when hallucination triggers exceed threshold.

sam: Agreed.

elaine: Thanks all — I'll post the draft scorecard + example gating JSON in #eng-ml-docs when ready.
